L16: ## 77.11 Universal flattening
L17: 
L18: This section is the analogue of More on Flatness, Section 【11†38.27】. Our main aim is to prove Lemma 【12†77.11.8】. However, we do not see a way to deduce this result from the corresponding result for schemes directly. Hence we have to redevelop some of the material here. But first a definition.
L19: 【13†Definition 77.11.1.】 Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module. We say that the universal flattening of $\mathcal{F}$ exists if the functor $F_{flat}$ defined in Situation 【14†77.7.8】 is an algebraic space. We say that the universal flattening of $X$ exists if the universal flattening of $\mathcal{O}_ X$ exists.
L20: This is a bit unsatisfactory, because here the definition of universal flattening does not agree with the one used in the case of schemes, as we don't know whether every monomorphism of algebraic spaces is representable (More on Morphisms of Spaces, Section 【15†76.4】). Hopefully no confusion will ever result from this.
L21: 【16†Lemma 77.11.2.】 Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces which is locally of finite type. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module of finite type. Let $n \geq 0$. The following are equivalent
L22: 
L23:   1. for some commutative diagram
L24: 
L25: \[ \xymatrix{ U \ar[d]_\varphi \ar[r] & V \ar[d] \\ X \ar[r] & Y } \]
L26: with surjective, étale vertical arrows where $U$ and $V$ are schemes, the sheaf $\varphi ^*\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $V$ in dimensions $\geq n$ (More on Flatness, Definition 【17†38.20.10】),
L27: 
L28:   2. for every commutative diagram
L29: 
L30: \[ \xymatrix{ U \ar[d]_\varphi \ar[r] & V \ar[d] \\ X \ar[r] & Y } \]
L31: 
L32: with étale vertical arrows where $U$ and $V$ are schemes, the sheaf $\varphi ^*\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $V$ in dimensions $\geq n$, and
L33:   3. for $x \in |X|$ such that $\mathcal{F}$ is not flat at $x$ over $Y$ the transcendence degree of $x/f(x)$ is $< n$ (Morphisms of Spaces, Definition 【18†67.33.1】).
L34: 
L35: If this is true, then it remains true after any base change $Y' \to Y$.
L36: Proof. Suppose that we have a diagram as in (1). Then the equivalence of the conditions in More on Flatness, Lemma 【19†38.20.9】 shows that (1) and (3) are equivalent. But condition (3) is inherited by $\varphi ^*\mathcal{F}$ for any $U \to V$ as in (2). Whence we see that (3) implies (2) by the result for schemes again. The result for schemes also implies the statement on base change. $\square$
L37: 【20†Definition 77.11.3.】 Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ which is locally of finite type. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module of finite type. Let $n \geq 0$. We say $\mathcal{F}$ is flat over $Y$ in dimensions $\geq n$ if the equivalent conditions of Lemma 【16†77.11.2】 are satisfied.
L38: 【21†Situation 77.11.4.】 Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ which is locally of finite type. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_ X$-module of finite type. For any scheme $T$ over $Y$ we will denote $\mathcal{F}_ T$ the base change of $\mathcal{F}$ to $T$, in other words, $\mathcal{F}_ T$ is the pullback of $\mathcal{F}$ via the projection morphism $X_ T = X \times _ Y T \to X$.
L39: Note that $f_ T : X_ T \to T$ is of finite type and that $\mathcal{F}_ T$ is an $\mathcal{O}_{X_ T}$-module of finite type (Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma 【22†67.23.3】 and Modules on Sites, Lemma 【23†18.23.4】). Let $n \geq 0$. By Definition 【20†77.11.3】 and Lemma 【16†77.11.2】 we obtain a functor
L40: 【24†77.11.4.1】
L41: 
L42: \begin{equation} \label{spaces-flat-equation-flat-dimension-n} F_ n : (\mathit{Sch}/Y)^{opp} \longrightarrow \textit{Sets}, \quad T \longrightarrow \left\{ \begin{matrix} \{ *\} & \text{if }\mathcal{F}_ T\text{ is flat over }T\text{ in }\dim \geq n, \\ \emptyset & \text{else.} \end{matrix} \right. \end{equation}
L43: In Situation 【21†77.11.4】 we sometimes think of $F_ n$ as a functor $(\mathit{Sch}/S)^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ endowed with a morphism $F_ n \to Y$. Namely, if $T$ is a scheme over $S$, then an element $h \in F_ n(T)$ is a morphism $h : T \to Y$ such that the base change of $\mathcal{F}$ via $h$ is flat over $T$ in $\dim \geq n$. In particular, when we say that $F_ n$ is an algebraic space, we mean that the corresponding functor $(\mathit{Sch}/S)^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ is an algebraic space.

L97@P6: S. Lichtenbaum.
L98@P6: Most of the known and expected properties of motivic cohomology (predicted
L99@P6: in [ABS87] and [Lic84]) can be divided into two families. The first family concerns
L100@P6: properties of motivic cohomology itself – there are theorems about homotopy invariance, Mayer-Vietoris and Gysin long exact sequences, projective bundles, etc.
